title: Research: exact P111 port-plane matching audit
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Adds an exact bounded factorization of the selected P111 bit decoder using a matching of 55 orthogonal port pairs and one residual port. The best of 751 two-edge-switch/residual-swap candidates has a scalar pairing-rank sum of 112, attained twice, and reproduces every entry of the 111-by-661 dirty map after an exact basis change. This is a local algebraic result, not a physical supplier or a κ improvement; the incumbent nine-line scalar charge is 63, and selected κ remains 0.001672660197076918.

The hypothetical `unpaid=221/111` relaxation passes `a=3/997` with at most 29 additional centre-charge units. That coverage value is assumed, and the remaining route, endpoint, hosting, precision and restoration costs are unknown.

## Task and overlap

Base: canonical `main` commit `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`. Task `coverage-law-change`, refined to test one exact port grouping on the selected P111 word before attempting physical implementation. The selected word, expected profile, prior dirty-map receipt and ceiling source are source-pinned in `research/p111-selected-plane-matching/SOURCES.json`.

[PR #1900](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1900) audits five fixed coefficient-space planes and a scalar charge of 73; it does not pair physical P111 ports. [Discussion #1587](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1587) records the outstanding source/target endpoint obligation. This contribution adds the bounded port-matching census and full dirty-map replay, but does not discharge that obligation.

## Validation

On CPython 3.12.15:

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/p111-selected-plane-matching --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/p111-selected-plane-matching
```

Both passed. The registered verifier uses exact F2 and rational arithmetic, checks all 73,371 dirty-map entries against the prior receipt, and rejects missing-residual and missing-plane-term controls. No native schedule, full supplier replay or Lean proof is claimed; those obligations are listed in the package.

## Credit

The selected bit word and its predecessor chain are credited in its [tuning package](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/tree/main/research/e8-bit-p111-tuned/tune). The inherited scalar pairing-rank model is documented in the [P111 copy-rank certificate](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/main/research/p111-copy-rank-certificate/PROOF.md). Prepared by Gonzalo Mier with OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

See the package's [two scoped follow-ups](https://github.com/Gonzalo-Mier/integer-mult-bounds/blob/research/p111-selected-port-plane-matching/research/p111-selected-plane-matching/README.md#open-next-questions): realize one winning plane at a legal cut with arbitrary dirty restoration, then price its complete interface and recursive bill against the conditional 29-unit margin.
